newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Yallouz sees Brazil coffee about 28 mln bags-trade.
newsitem.headline: Yallouz sees Brazil coffee about 28 mln bags-trade.

text.p: The latest private forecast of the Brazilian 1997/98 coffee crop by Leon Yallouz, former agronomist for U.S. Agriculture Department, is for a harvest of around 28 million 60-kg bags, traders said.
"It is about 28 million bags, higher than last time," a trader said.
Other traders said they had heard the figure was 28.6 million bags.
Yallouz could not be reached to comment on the reports.
Yallouz' previous forecast at the end of February was said to have been for 27.5 million bags although this has never been confirmed.
A 28 million bag plus estimate would be higher than most trade forecasts which are between 23 million and 25 million bags for the crop currently being harvested.

The greatest difference is in Yallouz' evaluation of the crop in Minas Gerais state which traders said he has plotted at over 15 million bags. Other estimates are around 10.5 million to 11 million bags.
The Brazilian government is working with around 22 million bags while the USDA recently issued its own first forecast of the 1997/98 crop of 28 million bags.
The USDA estimate caused an outcry not so much because of its size but because it plotted the harvest as higher than the crop in 1996/97 which it said reached 27.5 million bags.

Yallouz, after the USDA forecast, declined to comment on the 1997/98 figure but said he thought the 1996/97 figure was too low and that the harvest last year had been "somewhere over 28 million bags."
He did not give any figure for 1996/97 in his latest report, traders said.
